projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained high mobile presence (13-16 devices) paired with zero camera activity over four hours strongly indicates the cameras are offline, muted, or the family is congregating in a camera-blind zone, while the gradual device decline shows they are winding down for the evening. This warrants a quick system check to ensure cameras are functioning or confirm if a privacy/rest mode is active.

The sustained presence count of 14-20 devices on a Saturday evening, paired with zero camera activity, strongly suggests a social gathering or playdate is underway, though the lack of visual verification leaves the exact guest count unconfirmed. The stabilization around 15 devices aligns with the previously flagged gradual departure trend, indicating the event is winding down.

The steady decline in connected mobile devices from 21 to 15 over 72 minutes indicates a gradual departure, strongly suggesting the household or guests are leaving for the afternoon. This pattern is worth noting to proactively adjust security and climate settings before the home becomes unattended.
Steve slept only 3.21h last night. May be a rough morning — heads up.

The sustained connection of 17–20 mobile devices with zero motion or camera activity at nearly midnight strongly indicates overnight guests or a gathering, as the count far exceeds your household's typical footprint. Everyone appears settled and resting, but you may want to confirm if you're expecting visitors or if extra devices were left connected.

The sustained count of 14-20 connected devices with zero motion or camera activity at 10:51 PM strongly suggests either unmonitored guests in a camera-blind zone or a network artifact (e.g., a stuck IoT device). Steve should verify if he has overnight visitors or check for a malfunctioning smart device.

The sustained presence of 14-16 mobile devices paired with zero camera or motion activity strongly indicates a network presence detection glitch or unauthorized access rather than actual occupants, warranting a connectivity and security check.

The sustained count of 14-16 connected devices significantly exceeds the household's typical footprint, and combined with zero motion or camera activity over the past hour, strongly suggests either unmonitored guests occupying the home or a network/IoT device falsely reporting presence. A quick verification is recommended to rule out unauthorized access or a stuck smart device.

The sustained 13-16 connected devices paired with zero motion or camera activity strongly suggests the household is gathered in a single room for a Friday evening activity, or that devices are left unattended; this aligns with normal weekend routines but warrants a quick wellness check if the pattern persists past typical wind-down times.

The sustained presence of 14-19 mobile devices with zero corresponding camera, motion, or environmental activity strongly indicates a network tracking artifact (likely MAC randomization or guest network noise) rather than actual occupancy, which could lead to false automation triggers if unaddressed.
